precepts.text: Samuel's mentality as a leader: God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you; for a leader of Israel to stop praying for the nation is a transgression.
precepts.point: When the lords of the Philistines heard Israel was gathered at Mizpeh, they came up against Israel again, and Israel was afraid. But this time, instead of running for the ark, the children of Israel charged Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines. They knew the prayer of a righteous man reaches the ears of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
This is Samuel's mentality as a leader: “God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way.”

For a leader of Israel to stop praying for the nation is a transgression. So when the children of Israel said, “Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us”, they were asking of Samuel the very thing he held himself bound to do. He said, “I will pray for you unto the Lord”, and he did not cease.

precepts.text: He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel; the righteous acts Samuel rehearses are those acts.
precepts.point: It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now stand still, that Samuel may reason with them before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord which he did to them and to their fathers.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.”

Samuel told the people, “It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now therefore stand still, that I may reason with you before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord, which he did to you and to your fathers.” The righteous acts Samuel rehearses are those acts the Most High made known unto the children of Israel.

precepts.text: After Gideon led the three hundred, the men of Israel said, Rule thou over us, both thou and thy son and thy son's son also, for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.
precepts.point: So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
After Gideon led the three hundred, “the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son also: for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.”

Gideon is Jerubbaal, one of the deliverers Samuel names: “the Lord sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelled safe.” This is the history of the book of Judges. When Israel forgat the Lord their God, he sold them into the hand of Sisera, of the Philistines, and of the king of Moab; when they cried, “We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord, and have served Baalim and Ashtaroth”, he sent a deliverer.

The people wanted to make their deliverer a king. But none of those saviors had to wear a crown.

precepts.text: Gideon refused: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you; the Lord shall rule over you. He knew that if thrones were set up, the people would put their trust and faith in the king instead of the Most High; it was never the Lord's intention to set kings in the flesh over Israel, he was to be our king.
precepts.point: So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“And Gideon said unto them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the Lord shall rule over you.”

Gideon refused. He knew that if thrones were set up, the people would put their trust and faith in the king instead of the Most High. It was never the Lord’s intention to set kings in the flesh over Israel; he was to be our king.

That is Samuel’s point in rehearsing the deliverers. Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah and Samuel delivered Israel on every side, and Israel dwelled safe, without a crown. What Israel needed was not a king but to put away the idols. It is not just about having the ark of the covenant among you, as when Israel went and got the ark against the Philistines, got beat even worse, and lost the ark. You have to put away the idols and stop serving Baalim and Ashtaroth.

precepts.text: Moses prophesied Israel would come into the land and say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me.
precepts.point: Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Moses saw this coming long before it happened. In the spirit of the Lord he knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and he wrote it down ahead of time: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me”.

That is what Samuel is rebuking. When Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against them, Israel said, “Nay; but a king shall reign over us: when the Lord your God was your king.” They wanted a king they could see and touch, because all the nations around them had kings. That demand exposed their disbelief in the Lord, and Moses had already written it down.

precepts.text: The king must be one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
precepts.point: Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
The same law that foresaw the demand set its terms: “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.”

So when Samuel says, “behold, the Lord hath set a king over you”, the king stands under the law Moses wrote ahead of time: one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren, never a stranger.

precepts.text: His heart must not be lifted up above his brethren, and he must not turn aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children in the midst of Israel; that is exactly what Samuel just told the people.
precepts.point: Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
The law of the king ends on the very terms Samuel just laid before the people. The king must walk so “That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left: to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Israel.”

Samuel says the same: “If ye will fear the Lord, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God”. If you and your king do not rebel against the voice of the Lord, the ultimate king, you will be all right. The king who turns not aside prolongs his days in his kingdom, he and his children.

precepts.text: If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee.
precepts.point: But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers. Samuel repeats it because Israelites require repetition.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Then comes the other side: “But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

Samuel says it again: “But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers.” He repeats it because Israelites require repetition. The hand of the Lord against you is these curses coming upon you and overtaking you.

precepts.text: The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; if you and your king disobey, the Lord sends you and your king into subjection to the other nations.
precepts.point: But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers. Samuel repeats it because Israelites require repetition.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Among those curses the king himself is named: “The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.”

That is why Samuel puts the people and the king under the same warning. If you and your king disobey, the Lord sends you and your king into subjection to the other nations. The king they demanded so they could be like the nations would go down with them into the hands of the nations.

precepts.text: The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice; imagine how terrified they were when that voice went off.
precepts.point: Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel asks, “Is it not wheat harvest to day?” That was the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat, and Samuel called unto the Lord, “and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day”.

“The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.” Imagine how terrified they were when that voice went off over their harvest: “all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.”

precepts.text: And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them; that is the power the Most High put on display.
precepts.point: Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.” That is the power the Most High put on display that day.

The thunder and rain came when Samuel called, on the day it should have been clear, “that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king.”

precepts.text: This is really a precept for the just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; the fall does not end your service to the Most High.
precepts.point: Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Samuel does not tell Israel they did nothing wrong: “Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart”. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy.

This is really a precept for “a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” The fall does not end your service to the Most High. The just man rises up again and keeps following the Lord with all his heart.

precepts.text: What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?
precepts.point: Our people do the same thing today, icing out crosses and things of that nature that cannot do a thing for them; those are the vain things our people follow after. Samuel warned Israel not to do it, and over a span of time that is exactly what they ended up doing.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“And turn ye not aside: for then should ye go after vain things, which cannot profit nor deliver; for they are vain.” Something you make with your own hands is not going to make thunder and rain come on your harvest day to show you how wicked you are. Idols cannot help you or save you.

Samuel warned Israel not to do it, and over a span of time that is exactly what they ended up doing. The Lord asked through Jeremiah, “What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?” They walked after the vain things Samuel named, and became vain themselves.

Our people do the same thing today, icing out crosses and things of that nature that cannot do a thing for them. Those are the vain things our people follow after.

precepts.text: Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
precepts.point: Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“For the Lord will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake: because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people.” That is part of the comfort of the scriptures: he may purge his people, but he will never exterminate the Israelites, for his name’s sake.

Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, asks the question himself: “Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” And he gives himself as the proof: “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” Paul said the same thing Samuel said.

precepts.text: God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew; the Lord has not cast off Israel.
precepts.point: Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Paul goes on: “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” The Lord has not cast off Israel.

It pleased the Lord to make Israel his people in Samuel’s day, and after Christ they are still the people which he foreknew. He will not forsake them, for his great name’s sake.

precepts.text: Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God; restraining prayer shows you are starting to lack fear of the Most High. If you want him in your life, you cannot restrain prayer from him, any more than you would let communication die with someone you wanted to keep.
precepts.point: For those who battle with prayer, meditate on that: ceasing to pray for your nation puts you in sin.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Marinate on this verse: “Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way”. Samuel was a leader who loved his nation, and he says that if he stopped praying for them, that itself would put him in sin.

“Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.” Restraining prayer shows you are starting to lack fear of the Most High. If you want him in your life, you cannot restrain prayer from him, any more than you would let communication die with someone you wanted to keep.

For those who battle with prayer, meditate on that: ceasing to pray for your nation puts you in sin.
